description: Team of 3 CS students from Karachi building FlameLens — an AI-powered dashboard that searches and summarizes NASA’s microgravity combustion research to generate fire safety insights for space missions. Skills: Python, web development, AI/ML.
summary: FlameLens is a spacecraft fire safety research dashboard that makes NASA combustion data accessible and understandable. Built on 191 real NASA sources — 178 NTRS research papers, 24 PSI experiment records from BASS-II and SoFIE-GEL on the ISS, and 13 NASA web pages — it features five tools: a Fire Risk Calculator using real NASA-STD-6001B thresholds, Mission Scenarios comparing ISS, Moon, and Mars fire risk, a Cool Flame Visualizer animating NASA’s FLEX discovery, an Incident Timeline from Apollo 1 to SAFFIRE, and an AI-powered research assistant using Groq to synthesize cited answers from the paper database. All data gaps (Lunar, Mars) are honestly shown as NO DATA rather than fabricated. FlameLens bridges the gap between raw NASA research and mission planners who need to understand fire in space.
details:
FlameLens is a spacecraft fire safety research dashboard built on 191 real NASA sources. It addresses a critical gap: fire behaves fundamentally differently in microgravity — flames spread in all directions with no convection, survive at lower oxygen levels, and can persist invisibly as “cool flames” after appearing extinguished. Yet this research is scattered across hundreds of technical papers that most people can't access.

What it does:
FlameLens has five core tools — a Fire Risk Calculator using real NASA-STD-6001B thresholds that flags danger zones by oxygen %, pressure, and gravity; Mission Scenarios comparing fire risk across ISS, Moon, and Mars (with honest DATA GAP labels where no NASA data exists); a Cool Flame Visualizer animating NASA’s FLEX experiment discovery from the ISS; an Incident Timeline from Apollo 1 to SAFFIRE; and an AI research assistant powered by Groq (Qwen model) that searches 191 NASA paper abstracts and returns cited answers in seconds.

Data sources:
24 combustion records from NASA PSI (BASS-II and SoFIE-GEL ISS experiments), 178 paper abstracts from NASA NTRS, and 13 NASA web pages — stored in a Supabase vector database for semantic search.

Tech stack:
React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector), Groq AI API, deployed on Vercel.

Impact:
FlameLens makes a decade of ISS fire safety research understandable to engineers, students, and mission planners — and honestly shows where data gaps exist (Lunar, Mars) that future missions like NASA FM2 will need to fill.
